MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

This neuron has no clean semantic trigger — it fires weakly-to-moderately on ordinary mid-sentence continuation tokens (the final item of a list, the second half of a collocation like "American Girl", "derived from", "to be a member"), and is strongly *suppressed* on tokens that open a new line/headline after a newline or exclamation point ("!\n", "Need…", "Dep…", "An Or|ca"), so it mainly encodes "inside an ongoing clause" vs. "start of a new line".

L27·N8140unmasked layer
This neuron is essentially inhibitory (its whole corpus range is negative), and its strongest negative firing lands on function-word/punctuation tokens in flowing prose — especially a comma closing an introductory phrase right before a named subject ("As a result, Vysionics…", "In her free time, Doris…") or a linking "to" in a repeated address formula; its near-zero "top" activations are just tokens immediately preceding proper names/titles, i.e. absence of suppression rather than a distinct trigger.
